what_happened: Confirmed via grep that task-lock.sh's acquire_named_mutex family (scope/commit/gate-lock) uses mkdir-based atomicity, never flock -- the dispatch's 'flock behaves differently' concern does not apply to the extension path. Also found an existing XDG_RUNTIME_DIR-with-fallback precedent already in the codebase (hooks/tts-notify.sh's COOLDOWN_FILE), and confirmed on the live host that XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$UID is tmpfs, mode 700, owned by the user, and per systemd's pam_systemd(8) is created at first login and removed at final logout -- so an abandoned host-scoped lock there is reclaimed by OS logout/reboot independent of task-lock.sh's own staleness arithmetic.

Plan-time re-derivation confirmed every structural claim in the research report (three gate-acquire call sites; named-mutex uses mkdir + time-elapsed reclaim with no kill -0; test-gate-lock.sh's serialization case runs both invocations from one shared WORKDIR) and surfaced one registration surface the report did not name: agent-system/extensions/core/manifest.json enumerates every test file individually in provides.scripts[] and is sync-enforced by test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh, so the new suite needs a manifest row alongside its suite-classification.data row or it never reaches the deployed tests dir Gate 8 discovers.

Phase 3's Batch Gate Deferral narrowed verify-touched.sh pass (41 suites, scoped to tests/run-all.sh + verify-deploy.sh) reported 2 NEW failures: test-gate-slow-bucket-split.sh (case a: real discovered total reported as 0) and test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh (live-corpus violation naming .claude/scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-close-status-bind.sh, a discovered-but-unclassified, non-executable test file). Investigation confirmed both are attributable to task 651's concurrent, uncommitted in-flight work on this shared tree (its .return-meta.json and plan file are both modified-but-uncommitted at the time of this check; the new test file has no git history and no suite-classification.data row yet), not to this task's own edits -- this task never touches suite-classification.data, the slow-bucket hints logic, or any test-orchestrate-close-status-bind.sh file. This task's own edits were independently verified green via direct, isolated-fixture invocations (test-gate-lock.sh 27/27 twice, test-run-all-parallel.sh 12/12, a cross-directory --only-narrowed run touching neither lock root, and a stub-task-lock.sh fail-open smoke test producing a real verdict).

Phase 4's lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh direct run reported exactly 1 violation: test-orchestrate-close-status-bind.sh (task 651's uncommitted in-flight new test file, same as observed in Phase 3's verify-touched.sh pass). This task's own new suite, test-gate-lock-host-scope.sh, is NOT named in the violation output, confirming its suite-classification.data row (added this phase) is complete and correct.
